 Veterans Day is approaching, meaning Americans will see changes in bank hours and mail delivery next week.
 No matter the day of the week, November 11 is observed as a federal holiday each year to mark the day in 1918 when troops stopped fighting in World War I.
 Originally called Armistice Day when Congress declared the holiday in 1938 , Veterans Day honors all veterans, both living and dead, who served in the U.S. Armed Forces.
 Government offices, banks and post offices across the country are closed on the holiday, which falls on a Wednesday this year. Depending on the location, many public and private schools stay open, while some restaurants and stores offer deals and discounts for veterans.
 Veterans Day is one of 11 federal holidays observed this year.
